source_commit.identity_note: The local execution and fetched repository text were not treated as byte-identical because their SHA-256 hashes differ. Results are retained as independent estimator-mechanics diagnostic evidence, not exact-blob execution evidence.

root_failure_modes_eps_1e-4_ridge_1e-4_w.command: root-failure-mode diagnostic using the v4 estimator mechanics

null_definition.oracle: For each feature path and predeclared direction, solve the exact finite-sample equal-risk quadratic under the known AR(0.5)+heteroskedastic covariance.
null_definition.estimated: Fit nuisance mean/covariance components from the observed dataset, reconstruct the same finite-sample equal-risk quadratic, and use its positive root as the plug-in restricted null point.
null_definition.bootstrap: Generate dependent/heteroskedastic bootstrap outcomes from the estimated restricted null and evaluate every bootstrap world with the same rolling estimator and Bartlett studentizer.

interpretation.primary: The severe weak-direction failure is primarily null-surface topology, not nuisance estimation. At epsilon=1e-4 and ridge=1e-4, only about 42% of paths have a positive equal-risk root even with oracle nuisance; among oracle-supported paths, estimated nuisance retains a positive root on about 99.5% and shifts the root by about 3.3% in the median.
interpretation.calibration: On a root-supported near-singular control (epsilon=1e-3, ridge=1e-4, weak), 500x99 gives oracle rejection 5.6% and estimated-nuisance rejection 6.0%. This is encouraging mechanical calibration but far from a proof.
interpretation.severe_cell: At epsilon=1e-4, ridge=1e-4, weak, the 500x99 pilot has only 219 usable composite-null points. The oracle and estimated rejection rates are 4.11% and 3.20%, respectively, but the dominant limitation is that most feature paths do not admit the positive weak-direction null point in the first place.
interpretation.formal_boundary: No formal p-value, confidence interval, estimator compatibility claim, uniform size guarantee, or real-data result is established.

next_gate.name: least-favorable null-surface envelope
requirements: predeclare a finite direction grid or an analytically defined admissible surface parameterization before calibration;
measure null-root existence as a first-class support condition;
estimate nuisance at each null point and quantify root movement;
evaluate bootstrap rejection over the entire admissible null surface rather than one convenient point;
retain origin-local conditioning and projection-preservation gates;
treat any projected lane as a separate estimand.
next_gate.reason: A composite equal-risk null is not characterized by one directional root. Uniform calibration requires controlling the worst admissible null configuration rather than selecting a favorable point after seeing the result.
